title: Best free AI tool for creating games?
author: Ok-Response3312
selftext:
I have been using earlier rosebud ai and it was good, it write games with 90% what I imagined. But it is isnanely expensive. Earlier I buy 15$ plan, and then change it to unlimited in the last two days to avoid paying +2k$ (I paid only 200$) and tryhard for 2 days. Results were good, but they disabled this and I dont want to pay more time.  
So something free (if necessary then somehting under 12$/month) I want Claude 4.6 quality or better. My main game ideas is text based game with 30+ endings, strategy game with level system, battle 3D game with cool mechanics. Rosebud did that for me but not all assets was polished. I used average 200-400 request to make game playble but it doesnt even have saving system. So looking for best option to me, pls help me

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body:
Step 1 - Convert all your game documentation into .md files. Put them all in the root folder of your project. This is your game design, your narrative design, your art design, your music design, lore, characters, everything. If you haven't fully developed all those systems then you really need to create baseline documentation before this can work.

The best way to spec out missing systems is to prompt "Ask me 10-15 questions about \_\_\_\_\_\_ system. Use my responses to make a design .md  for the project.

Step 2 - Write a AGENTS.md. This will be where you clearly define the roles each AI agent has (if running multiple agents), along with instructions for the AI agents to only stick to their roles. I would recommend you ask AI to help you define the roles for each agent and then ask you 10 questions about the project and use those answers to write the AGENTS.md. 

If you're just using Claude  you'll already have a claude.md file in your project folder when you install the claude MCP (if you're new and don't know what an MCP is, its what allows AI to work directly inside your game project). Thats the same thing as an AGENTS.md, but it's just for claude. 

But honestly if you're only able to afford one subscription i'd recommend codex over claude at the moment.

I use two agents. Claude and Codex. Claude designs the car, Codex is the mechanic. Before I start a task i still double check with the AI agent and ask "is this a claude task, or a codex task?"

Step 3 - Write an IMPLEMENTATION.md. This is what the agents will use to "talk" to each other. After each change is made to the project the agents will log what was implemented so another agent can pick up where the previous agent left off. Your AGENTS.md that you wrote in step 2 needs to have rules for the AI agents to log what they have implemented after they make any changes or updates to the project.

I would recommend that you ask AI to write the IMPLEMENTATION.md. Give it a prompt like "I want the AI agents to be able to "talk" to each other. Write an implementation.md that the AI agents can use to stay updated on any project changes. That way they will be able to pick up where the other AI agents left off with clean handoffs"

You'll occasionally want to have all the agents audit the project and align all documentation to catch any fringe cases. I find that writing your own scaffolding for your project works better than relying on superpowers or skills.

Ultimately, you're going to be forging your own path. I find that the most powerful tools you have at your disposal are the windows snip tool Win key + Shift + S (for screenshotting error logs) and the simple prompt - 

"I need to develop a \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ system. Ask me 10-15 questions and use my answers to help determine the design and write a design document. Explain any follow up steps and terminology like I am 5 years old"

comments.author: Waste_Building9565
comments.body: for the text-based game with branching endings, Claude via the API with a coding assistant like Cursor is probably your cheapest bet since you only pay per token. Godot with an AI plugin handles 3D battle mechanics better than Rosebud did for assets. for concept art and storyboarding those 30+ endings visually, Mage Space handles that on a flat monthly rate.
